domains.title: A bounded language runtime from representation to execution

subtopics.title: Values and a portable bytecode image

objectives.text: Specify tagged int32, Boolean, nil and generation-checked object references without conflating a language value with C object bytes.
Encode and decode a bounded CVM1 image using explicit little-endian fields and failure-atomic loading.
Reject truncated, unsupported and oversized images and explain which checks belong before execution.
Separate instruction-boundary discovery from control-flow stack analysis over every function.
Reject malformed operands, interior or cross-function branches, wrong call arity and incompatible stack heights at joins.
Explain why accepted structural bytecode still needs runtime type, initialization, resource and termination checks.
Implement a bounded opcode dispatch loop with explicit stack effects and checked int32 operations.
Distinguish type, range, stack-capacity and bytecode-format errors using deliberate counterexamples.
Preserve a declared result/error boundary and explain why VM arithmetic cannot inherit C signed-overflow behavior.
Represent each invocation with an independent instruction position, local slots, initialization state and operand-stack base.
Implement direct calls and returns with checked arity and frame capacity without recursing through the C interpreter.
Explain recursive execution and demonstrate bounded exhaustion distinct from native stack exhaustion.
Scan explicit source spans and resolve bounded lexical names while rejecting unknown or duplicate function definitions.
Compile literals, lexical bindings and arithmetic into the declared bytecode and validate the emitted program.
Separate hosted compiler limits and source errors from runtime errors and preserve output on failed compilation.
Lower Boolean conditionals and loops into patched instruction-boundary branches with compatible stack joins.
Define mutable local assignment, sequencing and loop-result semantics without accidental host-language control behavior.
Demonstrate both a terminating source loop and an infinite guest loop bounded by fuel.
Build fixed pair objects in caller-owned storage and distinguish slot identity from generation identity.
Demonstrate arena exhaustion without pretending unreachable objects are reclaimed during that phase.
Specify reset invalidation, reference ownership and the transition to an explicit-root collector.
Trace live operand values, initialized frame locals and explicit temporary roots with a bounded iterative mark worklist.
Reclaim unreachable cycles while preserving rooted graphs and allocation-time C temporaries.
Reject stale references and explain collection-budget exhaustion before sweep and remaining stop-the-world limits.
Maintain separate guest-dispatch, garbage-collection and host-call budgets with explicit units.
Stop infinite guest loops and resource-exhausting programs with observable structured outcomes.
Explain why instruction fuel alone cannot bound verifier cost, compiler cost, GC latency or a blocking host callback.
Embed the VM through a narrow integer service callback with explicit capabilities and failure propagation.
Connect an already accepted store through fixed-key little-endian values without exposing arbitrary native calls.
Distinguish callback failure, uncertain persistence and guest completion when a service performs external work.

subtopics.title: One VM core across Linux, Thumb and a kernel

objectives.text: Build one VM core for hosted Linux and freestanding Thumb without compiling the source-language compiler into firmware.
Run the same portable bytecode in an emulated Cortex-M target and an independently implemented kernel environment.
Audit compiler helpers, startup, memory placement and host-service adapters while keeping emulator and physical-board claims separate.

subtopics.title: Runtime defense, mutation and delayed transfer

objectives.text: Defend the source-to-bytecode-to-execution provenance and distinguish tested anchors from complete runtime mastery.
Use independent malformed programs and fault mutations to challenge verifier, lifetime and resource claims.
Repeat a changed-capacity or changed-host-service task after a delay without consulting the prior implementation.

domains.title: Persistent storage engine and crash consistency

objectives.text: Encode and decode 4096-byte pages with explicit byte order, version, identity, count, bounds and CRC checks; explain why casting a struct cannot define this format.
Reject invalid key/value extents and corrupt page metadata before following references or changing caller outputs.
Distinguish fresh-image format from reopen; diagnose a changed identity, count, checksum or short block without silently constructing an empty tree.
Implement a four-entry clean page cache whose tags identify exact physical pages; keep transaction-owned dirty nodes outside the cache.
Invalidate cached home or WAL bytes on publication and checkpoint transitions, demonstrating a stale-generation counterexample when invalidation is removed.
Account separately for cache hits, backend reads and fixed memory bytes on repeated and conflicting-page traces.
Use unsigned length-delimited key order and right-child separator equality to derive every lookup decision, including embedded zeros and equal prefixes.
Implement bounded lookup and linked-leaf lower-bound scans with early-stop callbacks and unchanged outputs on missing or undersized results.
Cross-check tree descent, leaf order, reachability and allocation; reject a dangling reference or leaf cycle before exceeding the page bound.
Split full leaf and internal nodes while preserving separator minima, occupancy, child ownership and leaf links through root growth.
Make updates and failed page allocations preserve the declared transaction state; distinguish replacement from insertion of a new key.
Reproduce a split-propagation error and compare all keys with an independent map; report the implementation's O(P) separator refresh cost explicitly.
Derive sibling borrowing, merging and root contraction from minimum occupancy and separator invariants.
Implement deletion with leaf-link repair and allocation-bitmap page reuse without leaving a reachable free page or an unreachable allocated page.
Demonstrate left/right redistribution, multi-level merge and reuse after deletion; preserve whole-map equality against an independent oracle.
Bound transaction scratch memory and enforce one writer with no concurrent readers; explain why private dirty nodes must not reach home pages before commit.
Implement begin, abort and capacity rejection so an abandoned transaction leaves the committed logical map unchanged.
Separate clean cache, committed WAL view and transaction-owned nodes when diagnosing a leaked uncommitted update.
Derive the persistence order: invalidate the old marker and flush, write complete after-images and flush, then publish and flush the new commit marker.
Implement explicit committed, aborted/error and indeterminate outcomes; close the handle after an uncertain publication instead of permitting blind retry.
Kill the omitted-commit-flush variant and show why a failed response may accompany either complete persistence or no committed change.
Validate the complete committed WAL batch before installing any home page; flush homes before publishing alternate generation metadata.
Select valid metadata generations and delay WAL reclamation until the new checkpoint is durably discoverable.
Recover from an interrupted checkpoint and explain why early marker reclamation can destroy the only authoritative committed generation.
Reopen an established image by validating generations, commit marker and every required after-image before replay.
Implement idempotent full-page redo that can itself be interrupted and repeated without changing the recovered application map.
Reject corrupt committed input and failed recovery I/O while preserving the failure image; distinguish corruption from an admissible old-or-new crash result.
Implement stable/pending block state and reproducible crash cuts that model admitted reorder, partial persistence, tears and failed acknowledgments.
Compare complete recovered maps against the independent transaction oracle across commit, checkpoint and repeated-recovery cuts.
Record tested cut counts and persistence patterns, kill semantic mutants, and explain why finite representative schedules do not exhaust physical failure behavior.
Translate complete-page operations into bounded pread/pwrite loops that handle EINTR, positive short transfers, zero progress and errors.
Implement the existing-file fsync contract and demonstrate commit-close-reopen on a disposable preallocated image with platform failures reported explicitly.
Compute page traffic, flush count and write amplification separately from useful payload, cached host traffic, device operations and physical power-loss claims.
Connect narrow VM integer services to the existing store through bounded byte encoding and explicit transaction outcomes without exposing arbitrary pointers or paths.
Adapt kernel whole-page read/write/flush capabilities to an exclusive store image slice, preserving user-buffer validation and durability responsibilities.
Execute write, lost-response failure, restart and read through the application boundary; reconcile indeterminate results instead of assuming an error proves absence.

domains.title: A small isolated x86-64 operating system

subtopics.title: Boot contracts and the long-mode transition

objectives.text: Derive the machine-state and memory contract between GRUB, transition assembly and C.
Build and execute an original protected-to-long-mode transition with a correctly linked freestanding image.
Diagnose a deliberately broken entry/mapping assumption from the first supported machine-state divergence.

subtopics.title: Bounded boot information and memory reservations

objectives.text: Validate complete boot-tag and memory-map spans before interpreting fields.
Reserve boot-owned memory and give reserved overlaps precedence over available ranges.
Reject truncated or overflowing records while preserving the prior output contract.

subtopics.title: Serial diagnosis and normalized exception frames

objectives.text: Separate architectural and software-saved exception state.
Implement a normalized trap entry/return and bounded first-cause diagnostics.
Distinguish a recoverable user fault from a fatal kernel-mode exception.

subtopics.title: Physical frames and explicit page-table ownership

objectives.text: Derive and implement frame ownership and exhaustion invariants.
Construct explicit process mappings with zero-fill and bounded allocation rollback.
Explain when page-table and frame storage may be reclaimed after a context switch.

subtopics.title: Ring-3 isolation and guarded user storage

objectives.text: Construct separate address spaces with explicit user/supervisor and write/execute policy.
Demonstrate process isolation with both positive and negative machine-level observations.
Explain guard-page detection and the limits of a finite memory-safety campaign.

subtopics.title: Timer preemption with a nonpreemptible kernel

objectives.text: Separate scheduling policy from context-save and address-space-switch mechanisms.
Implement timer-driven round-robin user preemption with valid stack ownership.
Measure and explain latency introduced by a nonpreemptible kernel.

subtopics.title: Static ELF64 and a read-only boot archive

objectives.text: Validate the bounded ELF program-header contract before committing mappings.
Implement a checked named-span boot archive and zero-filled static image loader.
Distinguish the educational executable profile from general ELF and filesystem support.

subtopics.title: Bounded syscalls and revocable process handles

objectives.text: Define an explicit syscall ABI and checked copy-in/copy-out contract.
Implement process-local handle ownership, closure and generation rejection.
Demonstrate that untrusted argument rejection preserves kernel and peer state.

subtopics.title: Modern PCI virtio discovery and split queues

objectives.text: Decode the selected PCI capability and feature negotiation contracts.
Implement split-queue publication and completion ownership with bounded descriptors.
Explain transport-specific ordering and why volatile alone does not establish the complete DMA protocol.

subtopics.title: Block completion, flush and persistence boundaries

objectives.text: Separate request completion, buffer release and persistent-state claims.
Implement explicit bounded page/sector conversion and flush propagation.
Qualify reboot observations against the actual emulated backend failure model.

subtopics.title: Init, bounded console shell and teardown

objectives.text: Build init and a bounded shell against the custom ABI rather than hosted libc.
Test interactive input and process teardown through actual guest execution.
Defend the boundary between a boot archive, shell and general process/filesystem services.

subtopics.title: One portable VM core inside a user process

objectives.text: Port the unchanged portable VM through explicit user-space adapters.
Reconcile VM, compiler-helper and process resource contracts.
Demonstrate runtime error and host-call budget behavior inside the original OS.

subtopics.title: VM, durable store and kernel reboot integration

objectives.text: Compose runtime, transaction and block interfaces without bypassing ownership layers.
Execute bytecode-to-durable-storage and reboot recovery on the original OS.
Explain lost-response ambiguity without equating a reported error to absence of commit.

subtopics.title: Kernel diagnosis, negative controls and delayed transfer

objectives.text: Use independent host and machine-level evidence to diagnose an original kernel defect.
Preserve matching source/image/tool identities and reject inadequate negative controls.
Transfer the mechanism to a delayed changed-condition assessment with explicit limits.
